rules.statement: A contract of tenancy does not require a written agreement but must include the identity of the premises, the period of tenancy, and the rent payable.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) A contract of Tenancy need not be in writing; the parties must be agreed on the identity of the premises, the period of Tenancy and the Rent Payable. (2) The best test of establishing Tenancy is proof of payment of Rent and the best evidence of payment of Rent is Rent Receipts. 222 (3) S. 52(2) read with S. 48(1) of the Partition Law and S. 14(1) of the Rent Act required Court to determine (i) whether the petitioners had entered into occupation of the premises as Tenants prior to the date of the Final Decree. (ii) whether they were entitled to continue in occupation of the premises as Tenants under the original 1st Respondent. The Petitioners had failed to satisfy Court of the matters aforesaid
